concepts.def: This part of the course brings philosophy of religion and ethical studies into conversation with the beliefs and practices of the religion you have studied.

concepts.term: Religion and the problem of evil
concepts.def: A dialogue examines how far evil and suffering challenge the studied religion's idea of God, and how its theodicies and practices respond.
Dialogues ask whether the religion treats visions, conversion and mysticism as authoritative revelation or tests such claims against scripture and tradition.
Believers locate ethical guidance in sacred texts, leaders, conscience and reason, and dialogues examine how these interact with secular moral philosophy.
Dialogues assess how far approaches such as natural moral law, situation ethics or virtue ethics are compatible with the religion's own moral teaching.
Strong answers weigh whether philosophical and ethical challenges strengthen, modify or undermine religious belief, reaching a justified judgement.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Dialogues between Philosophy & Religion / Ethical Studies & Religion — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Dialogues between Philosophy & Religion / Ethical Studies & Religion brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Dialogues between Philosophy & Religion / Ethical Studies & Religion.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the 'dialogues' element of the course require you to do?
options: Relate philosophy of religion and ethical studies to the teachings of the religion you have studied
Memorise the practices of six world religions
Study secular philosophy with no reference to religion
Compare the specifications of two exam boards

mcqs.q: Which question is an example of a dialogue between philosophy and religion?
options: How far does the problem of evil challenge this religion's understanding of God?
In what year was a particular church council held?
How many chapters are in a sacred text?
Which festivals occur in spring?

mcqs.q: Which question is an example of a dialogue between ethical theory and religion?
options: Is situation ethics compatible with the religion's moral teaching?
What is the population of religious believers worldwide?
When was the religion's founder born?
Which translation of scripture is oldest?

mcqs.q: What makes a strong evaluative answer in dialogues questions?
options: Weighing arguments for and against compatibility and reaching a justified judgement
Listing as many scholars as possible without comment
Asserting personal faith as conclusive proof
Avoiding any criticism of religious positions

mcqs.q: Does 'dialogue' mean you must prove religion either true or false?
options: Dialogues questions want students to demonstrate that religion is false (or true).
Dialogues questions are about conversations between two religious leaders.
No - it means examining how the religion responds to philosophical and ethical challenges; responses may strengthen, adapt or resist belief, and your task is evaluation.
Philosophy was invented to replace religion in the twentieth century.

mcqs.q: Are philosophy and religion automatically opposed to each other?
options: Philosophy was invented to replace religion in the twentieth century.
Philosophy and religion are necessarily enemies, so dialogue is impossible.
No - there are long traditions of using reason within faith, such as Aquinas's natural theology; 'faith versus reason' is one position in the debate, not an established fact.
Only quotations from scripture can earn marks in dialogues answers.

mcqs.q: Is describing both topics side by side enough for high marks?
options: No - dialogues demand genuine connection and evaluation: showing how the philosophical or ethical material bears on the religion's claims and judging the outcome.
Only quotations from scripture can earn marks in dialogues answers.
Writing everything you know about both topics earns the evaluation marks.
Philosophy was invented to replace religion in the twentieth century.

free_texts.q: Name the Greek philosopher of the Theory of Forms.
free_texts.hint: Student of Socrates, teacher of Aristotle.

sequence.def: Republic, c.375 BC: true reality is the eternal world of Forms
c.350 BC: explanation of change, ending in the Prime Mover
Proslogion, 1078: God is that than which nothing greater can be conceived
Summa Theologica, 1274: a posteriori proofs from motion and cause
1779: attacks the design and causal arguments
Critique of Practical Reason, 1788: God postulated for morality
